_README: Q97 systematic audit of every mappings/subjects/*_volume_mapping.json entry with atlas_id: null and a note
expressing qualitative doubt ("not trusted", "fragment", "review", etc.) rather than an already-
established hard quantitative fact, following up on Q96's platysma reversal. A future pass can resume
from this file rather than re-running the full grep sweep -- see PROJECT_STATE Q97 for the narrative.
search_method: grepped every mappings/subjects/*_volume_mapping.json for atlas_id:null entries, then filtered notes for qualitative-doubt language (not trusted, fragment, review, questionable, uncertain, unreliable, revisit, small, low-confidence, etc.) with no specific number already pinning down the verdict. 64 keyword hits found; almost all of them turned out to already cite a specific measured number (a voxel/cm3 count, a component-analysis result, a stated expected range) that already settles the question -- these are NOT candidates by this audit's own bar, just verbose settled notes. Only ct_vhf_left_forearm's 20 review-pending entries (Q71, dated one day before this audit) were genuinely still-open judgment calls; of those, 5 were verified and shipped, the other 15 checked and confirmed still correctly declined.

entries.doubt_expressed: rule-based; compartment holding supinator, anconeus (8.3 cm3), not split: Supinator (7.6 cm3) and anconeus (0.7 cm3) at the proximal end: the anconeus region is far too small to be the muscle, and the supinator wraps the radius where its border with the mobile wad is the position rule line, not a septum.
entries.q97_evidence: Note already states a specific, already-established quantitative fact (a measured fragment/voxel size, a component-analysis result, a specific volume outside a stated expected range, or a specific L/R mismatch) rather than an informal pre-toolkit doubt -- does not meet this audit's candidate bar (contrast with Q96's platysma, which had no number attached at all). Not re-verified this session; left as-is.

entries.doubt_expressed: 2.7 cm3 (was ~1.0/0.9 before a numpy-casting bug fix in floor_rules() -- unrelated code path, fixed 2026-09-18 -- happened to also re-run the whole script); the TOTAL volume is now inside the expected range, but connected-component analysis on the label volume shows it is NOT one piece: 24 disconnected islands, largest one only 26% of the total -- confirmed on the volume BEFORE the fix too (9-13 islands, 31-48% largest), so this is a pre-existing property of the strap_compartment/strap_rules segmentation, not a regression. A plausible total volume made of a dozen disconnected blobs is not a continuous strap muscle; still NOT SHIPPED. Kept in the label volume for review.
